intent: The caption of a SelectGroup, shown above its options and used as the group's accessible name.
typical_uses: A section caption such as a continent above its regions

dont_use_when.situation: The caption naming the whole select field

invariants.text: Rendering the label outside a SelectGroup throws; the primitive looks up the group it labels from context.
The label gives its id to the enclosing group's `aria-labelledby`; it is not an option, so it cannot be chosen and arrow keys skip it.

anti_patterns.dont: Use a disabled SelectItem as a section caption
anti_patterns.do_instead: Use a SelectLabel inside a SelectGroup; a disabled item is still reached by arrow keys and announced as an option

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the label's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the label's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (an empty object for a label). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through select.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A caption over a section of options

bad.title: A label straight under the popup
bad.why: There is no group for the label to name, so the primitive throws; wrap both in a SelectGroup.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, SelectGroupLabelState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the label's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: SelectGroupLabelState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the label's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (an empty object for a label). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through select.module.css, not through this.
